resource.name: General Building Permits
resource.description:
List of issued building permits from the City of Edmonton - Urban Planning & Economy Department for the public to do construction or maintenance on a structure located in the City. Note - All records start from January 1, 2009.
Please note : the decision was made to not release applicant information on this dataset as it was seen as a potential privacy issue. For instance, if a high profile member of the public were to apply for a permit, their name (and consequently address) would show up on this table and become easily searchable by the public.  We viewed this as a potential issue and decided to publish the dataset without applicant information.

resource.name: 24 Hour Rainfall Totals and Storm Severity Ratings
resource.description:
Rainfall is measured to assess storms and their effects on flooding and sewer performance and design.

Rainfall location color icons indicate rainfall totals and maximum storm rating during the past 24 hours. Data is sent once 2mm is accumulated in each gauge, so timing will vary.

Website is updated every 15 minutes. Higher storm ratings and rainfall totals may have occurred if a storm lasts more than 24h. Storm ratings and rainfall are based on data at the gauge location only - nearby areas may experience differing conditions due to variability of rainstorms.

Rainfall is measured between May and October; snowfall is not measured.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS176
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS176

Latitude: 53.440402
Longitude: -113.429593

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
columns_description: The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).    NOTE:  - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable.  Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS187
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS187

Latitude: 53.60563
Longitude: -113.4791

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
columns_description: The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable.  Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).    NOTE:  - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS108
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS108

Latitude: 53.54453
Longitude: -113.57793

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
columns_description: A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).   NOTE: - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable.  Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.

resource.name: Zoning Overlays
resource.description:
An overlay is a set of additional zoning rules that are applied to specific and
special areas around the city. An overlay can override or add to the rules of the
underlying zones.

Two examples of these are the North Saskatchewan River Valley and Ravine System Protection Overlay and the Mature Neighbourhood Overlay.

The North Saskatchewan River Valley and Ravine System Protection Overlay applies along the banks of the river and its ravines. The overlay makes sure that there is a development setback from the North Saskatchewan River Valley and Ravine System.

The Mature Neighbourhood Overlay (MNO) applies to Edmonton’s mature neighbourhoods. Created in 2001, the MNO is a part of the Zoning Bylaw that helps new development fit in with existing older communities that feature tree-lined streets and smaller lots. The current Mature Neighbourhood Overlay contains 24 regulations that modify the existing zoning, including more specific regulations for the amount of space between buildings and property lines, window placement and driveway locations, among other things.

For more information please see https://www.edmonton.ca/city_government/bylaws/zoning-bylaw.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS150
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS150

Latitude: 53.414184
Longitude: -113.494995

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
columns_description: The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).   NOTE: - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable.  Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.

resource.name: 2014 Census - Dwelling Unit By Language (Ward)
resource.description: All Census information is as of April 1, 2014. No data on any individual residence will be released.  To protect the privacy of individuals, data is compiled and presented at the city, ward and neighbourhood level only.  Neighbourhood results with a population under 49 are not posted to protect the information collected.  The designation of “No Response” includes households from which no census data could be collected or only partial data was available.  “Other Residential” includes dwelling units not covered by the other categories, such as a unit attached to a non-residential structure (e.g. an apartment in a store or church) or a movable structure (e.g. recreational vehicle, tent, etc.).

domain_metadata.value: Current, reliable census data is an essential tool available to the City of Edmonton, and all census data consumers, that will enable them to meet current and future challenges.  The data allows consumers to anticipate and adapt to change.  Basing decisions on constantly updated demographics results in more appropriate use of revenue and resources, allowing consumers to be proactive in their response to multiple demands, shifts in priorities and rapid changes that the future will bring.  With changes being made to collection of federal census data, consistent collection of municipal census data will be the most reliable source of comparative data available to the City of Edmonton.  Current census data will also allow the City to maximize per capita grants provided by the provincial and federal governments.

resource.name: Micromobility Trips
resource.description: The micromobility e-scooters and e-bikes trips in this dataset occurred on or after June 3, 2022. Individual trips that have a reported duration of less than 30 seconds or a reported distance of less than 100 metres have been excluded. Trip start times have been generalized to 1-hour intervals by truncation, and have been converted to local time. Trip origins and destinations have been generalized by tiling the city with hexagonal bins using the H3 library by Uber Technologies, Inc. Centrepoints and polygons are provided. Provider (vendor) names have been withheld. Trip IDs are hashed.

COVID-19 vaccines are safe, effective and save lives. The vaccine helps prevent you from getting infected and protects you from getting severely sick if you do get it.

Albertans are being vaccinated as fast as supply allows. This is happening in phases so people most at risk get it first. More groups will be eligible as we get more doses.

resource.name: 2012 Census - Population By Structure Type (Neighbourhood)
resource.description: All Census information is as of April 1, 2012. No data on any individual residence will be released.  To protect the privacy of individuals, data is compiled and presented at the city, ward and neighbourhood level only.  Neighbourhood results with a population under 49 are not posted to protect the information collected.  The designation of “No Response” includes households from which no census data could be collected or only partial data was available.  “Other Residential” includes dwelling units not covered by the other categories, such as a unit attached to a non-residential structure (e.g. an apartment in a store or church) or a movable structure (e.g. recreational vehicle, tent, etc.).

domain_metadata.value: Current, reliable census data is an essential tool available to the City of Edmonton, and all census data consumers, that will enable them to meet current and future challenges.  The data allows consumers to anticipate and adapt to change.  Basing decisions on constantly updated demographics results in more appropriate use of revenue and resources, allowing consumers to be proactive in their response to multiple demands, shifts in priorities and rapid changes that the future will bring.  With changes being made to collection of federal census data, consistent collection of municipal census data will be the most reliable source of comparative data available to the City of Edmonton.  Current census data will also allow the City to maximize per capita grants provided by the provincial and federal governments.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS204
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS204

Latitude: 53.474214
Longitude: -113.459777

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
columns_description: System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable.  Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).    NOTE:  - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.

domain_metadata.value: To share with the public the collection of speed data at the various locations throughout Edmonton.

resource.name: Pet License History by Neighbourhood
resource.description:
Pet license (cats, dogs, pigeons) transaction history by neighbourhood; details initial license issuance, periodic renewals, and the current (as of the dataset refresh date) status of the license (still an "issued" status, has expired, etc.).

Explanation of pet license statuses:

 - Issued: Up-to-date license
 - Delinquent: More than one month overdue
 - Renewed: License is in the last month before it expires, and the renewal notice has been sent
 - NSF: A cheque was received as payment, but was returned as NSF (not sufficient funds) by the bank
 - Expired: Less than one month overdue
 - Accepted: Pet licence account has been created but payment has not yet been applied to the account (used for brand new accounts)

NB: For FOIP reasons, pets are excluded from this dataset if there are fewer than five of the relevant animal type in the pet's neighbourhood. For example, if there are only four dogs in a particular neighbourhood, none of those dogs will be featured in this dataset.

domain_metadata.value: Current, reliable census data is an essential tool available to the City of Edmonton, and all census data consumers, that will enable them to meet current and future challenges.  The data allows consumers to anticipate and adapt to change.  Basing decisions on constantly updated demographics results in more appropriate use of revenue and resources, allowing consumers to be proactive in their response to multiple demands, shifts in priorities and rapid changes that the future will bring.  With changes being made to collection of federal census data, consistent collection of municipal census data will be the most reliable source of comparative data available to the City of Edmonton.  Current census data will also allow the City to maximize per capita grants provided by the provincial and federal governments.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS119
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS119

Latitude: 53.62285
Longitude: -113.39913

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.

resource.name: On-street Construction and Maintenance
resource.description:
Dataset summarizes active On-Street Construction and Maintenance (OSCAM) permits issued for the temporary use of road space for construction and special event activities. The dataset is current for the date the data is extracted. It does not provide historical or future OSCAM permit dates.

Data is broken into 4 categories:

- Permits that are successfully translated and/or cross referenced to actual road segments
- Permits that could not be cross referenced to actual road segements, but a good approximation could be drawn
- Permits that are successfully translated to only a point on the roadway network
- Permits that could not be translated or cross reference to any aspect of the road network

The criteria used to extract data:

- start date must be before the current date (and later than Jan 1, 2014)
- finish date must be later than current date, or empty
- status is completed (COMPLD)

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS104
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS104

Latitude: 53.52143
Longitude: -113.45936

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
columns_description: The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).   NOTE: - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable.  Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.

resource.name: Edmonton Business Census
resource.description: The dataset is a collection of business information, including business names, geographical locations, and the specific sectors and industries they belong to. The dataset is a valuable resource for anyone interested in exploring, analyzing, or understanding the diverse landscape of businesses in Edmonton. Some of the information include the North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code - a standardized system used to classify businesses and industries in North America. These codes, ranging from two to six digits, provide a comprehensive framework for classifying establishments based on their primary economic activities.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS007
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS007

Latitude: 53.489621
Longitude: -113.681505

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.

resource.name: 2012 Census - Dwelling Unit By Ownership (Ward)
resource.description: All Census information is as of April 1, 2012.  Ages of residents are effective April 1, 2012.  No data on any individual residence will be released.  To protect the privacy of individuals, data is compiled and presented at the city, ward and neighbourhood level only.  Neighbourhood results with a population under 49 are not posted to protect the information collected.  The designation of “No Response” includes households from which no census data could be collected or only partial data was available.  Bulk-count data from multiple-resident facilities (such as group homes, transient drop-in centres, residential hotels or criminal detention centres) may be limited when personal information cannot be obtained (i.e. information is not available or cannot be released by the facility administration).

domain_metadata.value: Current, reliable census data is an essential tool available to the City of Edmonton, and all census data consumers, that will enable them to meet current and future challenges.  The data allows consumers to anticipate and adapt to change.  Basing decisions on constantly updated demographics results in more appropriate use of revenue and resources, allowing consumers to be proactive in their response to multiple demands, shifts in priorities and rapid changes that the future will bring.  With changes being made to collection of federal census data, consistent collection of municipal census data will be the most reliable source of comparative data available to the City of Edmonton.  Current census data will also allow the City to maximize per capita grants provided by the provincial and federal governments.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS215
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS215

Latitude: 53.507072
Longitude: -113.486055

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
columns_description: The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).    NOTE:  - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable.  Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS095
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS095

Latitude: 53.5519
Longitude: -113.47297

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
columns_description: The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit. Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The Speed Unit of Measure. Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable. Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded. The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes. Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp. This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number. Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin. NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).   NOTE:  - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number. Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin. NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters. This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS210
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS210

Latitude: 53.5666
Longitude: -113.43092

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.

Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
columns_description: The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).    NOTE:  - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable.  Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS073
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS073

Latitude: 53.518169
Longitude: -113.475383

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.

Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
columns_description: The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

resource.name: 2012 Census - Population By School Residency (Neighbourhood)
resource.description: All Census information is as of April 1, 2012. No data on any individual residence will be released.  To protect the privacy of individuals, data is compiled and presented at the city, ward and neighbourhood level only.  Neighbourhood results with a population under 49 are not posted to protect the information collected.  The designation of “No Response” includes households from which no census data could be collected or only partial data was available.  “Other Residential” includes dwelling units not covered by the other categories, such as a unit attached to a non-residential structure (e.g. an apartment in a store or church) or a movable structure (e.g. recreational vehicle, tent, etc.).

domain_metadata.value: Current, reliable census data is an essential tool available to the City of Edmonton, and all census data consumers, that will enable them to meet current and future challenges.  The data allows consumers to anticipate and adapt to change.  Basing decisions on constantly updated demographics results in more appropriate use of revenue and resources, allowing consumers to be proactive in their response to multiple demands, shifts in priorities and rapid changes that the future will bring.  With changes being made to collection of federal census data, consistent collection of municipal census data will be the most reliable source of comparative data available to the City of Edmonton.  Current census data will also allow the City to maximize per capita grants provided by the provincial and federal governments.

resource.name: Land Parcels: Title Parcels (Point)
resource.description:
This dataset contains centroid point geometry for all Title Parcels in the City of Edmonton. Title parcels show property ownership, as described on the Certificate of Title.

The City of Edmonton has shifted the delivery of legal and title parcel mapping to the provincial government and their designated partners.  As of November 1st, 2021, the City will no longer provide datasets with land parcel boundary polygon geometry. Alberta Data Partnerships (ADP) - http://abdatapartnerships.ca - and their joint venture partner AltaLIS - https://www.altalis.com - now have the responsibility for making this information available for most of the province, including within the City of Edmonton.

Please see our Digital Map Products website https://www.edmonton.ca/business_economy/purchase_maps_aerial_photographs/digital-products for more information.

resource.name: 2014 Census - Previous Residence If Less Than One Year (Citywide)
resource.description: All Census information is as of April 1, 2014. No data on any individual residence will be released.  To protect the privacy of individuals, data is compiled and presented at the city, ward and neighbourhood level only.  Neighbourhood results with a population under 49 are not posted to protect the information collected.  The designation of “No Response” includes households from which no census data could be collected or only partial data was available.  “Other Residential” includes dwelling units not covered by the other categories, such as a unit attached to a non-residential structure (e.g. an apartment in a store or church) or a movable structure (e.g. recreational vehicle, tent, etc.).

domain_metadata.value: Current, reliable census data is an essential tool available to the City of Edmonton, and all census data consumers, that will enable them to meet current and future challenges.  The data allows consumers to anticipate and adapt to change.  Basing decisions on constantly updated demographics results in more appropriate use of revenue and resources, allowing consumers to be proactive in their response to multiple demands, shifts in priorities and rapid changes that the future will bring.  With changes being made to collection of federal census data, consistent collection of municipal census data will be the most reliable source of comparative data available to the City of Edmonton.  Current census data will also allow the City to maximize per capita grants provided by the provincial and federal governments.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS047
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS047

Latitude: 53.622776
Longitude: -113.531953

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.

domain_metadata.value: Current, reliable census data is an essential tool available to the City of Edmonton, and all census data consumers, that will enable them to meet current and future challenges. The data allows consumers to anticipate and adapt to change. Basing decisions on constantly updated demographics results in more appropriate use of revenue and resources, allowing consumers to be proactive in their response to multiple demands, shifts in priorities and rapid changes that the future will bring. With changes being made to collection of federal census data, consistent collection of municipal census data will be the most reliable source of comparative data available to the City of Edmonton. Current census data will also allow the City to maximize per capita grants provided by the provincial and federal governments.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS068
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS068

Latitude: 53.59497
Longitude: -113.54106

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
columns_description: A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number.  Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin.  NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit.  Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable.  Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The Speed Unit of Measure.  Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded.  The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes.  Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp.  This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters.  This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).   NOTE: - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

resource.name: Green
resource.description:
The depth layer that this spatial data represents is the < 0.35 m Surface Ponding Depth (Green) layer.

This map representation was created as a result of a 2013 to 2016 study done for the Edmonton area to determine the vulnerable areas of Edmonton in regards to a 1 in 100 year rainfall event.

Due to the constant changing of subsurface infrastructure (adding, upgrading, etc.) combined with the constant changing definition of a 1 in 100 year rainfall event (based on historic rainfall amounts), this raster file reflects the results of a study done in 2016 and should neither suggest previous year’s vulnerabilities nor future year’s vulnerabilities.

There are four different colours to show the depth of water that might pool on the ground during a large rainstorm.

Those colours are:

Green (representing a ponding depth from 0.00 - 0.35 m)
Yellow (representing a ponding depth from 0.35 - 0.50 m)
Orange (representing a ponding depth from 0.50 to 0.75 m)
Red (representing a ponding depth greater than 0.75 m)

For a more information regarding the Flood Risk Maps and the City’s proactive strategy see :
https://www.edmonton.ca/city_government/documents/RoadsTraffic/City-wide_Flood_Mitigation_Study.pdf

This dataset is based on 2014 information and will not be updated further. The model is based on a theoretical, worst-case scenario storm that has never occurred in the Edmonton area.

Model Accuracy:

For Areas west and central Digital Elevation Model was used from 2004.  For the rest of the areas Bare Earth LiDar data was used.  The surface data used was set to a horizontal resolution of 2.5 meters with a grid cell of 5m by 5m.  This puts the vertical resolution at an accuracy of 0.1 meters. 

This is a spline fit interpolations model.  This is a 1D-1D model with 2D interpolations.The accuracy of the information provided in these data sets is plus or minus 10 cm vertically, and 10 cm horizontally.   

The 100 year flood was based on the 2015 Edmonton 4 year Chicago storm event over 20 plus neighbourhoods.  The data is a collection of the worst case scenario of model runs.  
This is a common practice for Edmonton drainage models.  These models are high level concept and projects determined from this data set will undergo finer, more detailed modeling.

Disclaimer: No Warranty with Flood Risk Maps.
Your use of the flood risk maps is solely at your own risk, and you are fully responsible for any consequences arising from your use of the flood risk maps. The flood risk maps are provided on an “as is” and “as available” basis, and you agree to use them solely at your own risk. There are no warranties, expressed or implied in respect to the flood risk maps or your use of them, including without limitation, implied warranties and conditions of merchantability and fitness for any particular purpose.
Please note that the flood risk maps have been modified from their original source, and that all data visualization on maps are approximate and include only records that can be mapped.

resource.name: Driver Feedback Sign - DFS041
resource.description:
Driver Feedback Sign DFS041

Latitude: 53.544815
Longitude: -113.565714

The City has a number of Driver Feedback Signs (DFS) installed around the city. These units collect data as traffic approaches them and in some cases may display a message or a speed that is being detected. Also, these units are radar based and can only track one vehicle at a time (strongest signal).

Due to the number of DFS installations combined with the volume of data collected, each DFS has its own dataset.

Details of how the data is collected by the DFS are as follows:
- Data is accumulated and reported in 15 minute intervals
- Vehicle speeds are captured/reported in speed intervals (bins)
- Speed range/interval for the bins are determined by parameters/settings set for the DFS (Minimum/Maximum Speed Detection Setting)
- Two speed values are recorded for every vehicle - a Highest Speed Detected and a Slowest Speed Detected (explaining why there are two vehicle counts)
- The bins go from Bin 1 to Bin 10. Bin 1 can also be referred to a LO BIN and Bin 10 can also be referred to as HIGH BIN.

Things to note:

DFS devices are not to be used as or confused with traffic counters, as they are not.
DFS devices have a minimum detectable speed of approximately 6 km/hr.
DFS devices have a maximum (theoretical) detectable speed of approximately 225 km/hr.
DFS devices are programmable with different parameters that can also follow a timed schedule.
columns_name: Vehicle Count at Highest Speed Detected
Vehicle Count at Slowest Speed Detected
columns_description: The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected fastest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.

The number of vehicles that were successfully detected and recorded within the specified parameters. This Vehicle Count is not and should not be correlated to a traffic volume count within the 15 minute interval.

The Timestamp of when the data was recorded. The time interval between recordings is 15 minutes. Note: It is possible to not have a specific recording of data at a specific Timestamp. This can occur for a number of reasons; however, the data values are still for the 15 minute interval.

A value between 1 and 10, representing the data bin for which the vehicle count and the speed range is applicable. Bin 1 records the number of vehicles that were detected to travel in the slowest speed range and Bin 10 would be for the fastest speed range.
A unique ID assigned to the location for proper/accurate identification.
The Speed Unit of Measure. Note: The usual setting is KPH but could also be MPH.
The direction of travel of vehicles that are being detected by the DFS unit.
System generated ID to eliminate the possibility of duplicate data.

A calculated value based on (Maximum Speed Detection Setting and Minimum Speed Detection Setting).   NOTE:  - For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH. - For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

A flag value that indicates the following: 0 - if the both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are below the Speed Limit 1 - if the Speed Limit is between the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin 2 - if the value of both the Minimum Speed and Maximum Speed for the Bin are greater than the Speed Limit

The fastest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number. Vehicles can travel less than or equal to this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin. NOTE: For Bin 10, the maximum detectable speed is approximately 225 KPH.

The slowest detected speed travelled that corresponds to the Bin Number. Vehicles can travel equal to or faster than this speed for it to be recorded for the Bin. NOTE: For Bin 1, the minimum detectable speed is approximately 6 KPH.

The number of vehicles counted in the 15 minute time interval where the detected slowest speed of the vehicle was equal to or greater than the Minimum Speed for the Bin and is less than or equal to the Maximum Speed for the Bin.
The fastest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
The lowest speed setting for the DFS Unit used to determine the speed ranges for each Bin.
A brief / abbreviated description of the location where the DFS unit is located.
The Speed Limit setting for the DFS unit. Note: This may not be the enforceable speed for the roadway.
